Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

graphlearnR 0.1.0

Initial release. graphlearnR provides graph machine learning for R on top of the torch package: graph data structures, message passing layers, model builders, training and evaluation, sampling for large graphs, heterogeneous and temporal graphs, graph transformers, and explainability.

Graph data

  • graph_data() stores homogeneous graphs with 1-based edge_index, node and edge features, labels, weights, masks, and node identifiers. Undirected input is given once per pair and stored in both directions.
  • Conversion to and from igraph, edge lists, and dense or sparse adjacency matrices; graph_tensors() moves a graph to torch tensors on any device.
  • graph_batch() and unbatch() combine graphs into one disconnected graph and split them again.
  • Transforms for self loops, duplicate edges, induced subgraphs, symmetrization, feature normalization, and degree features.
  • Validation of graph structure, and a shared feature schema for datasets (graph_schema()).

Layers and message passing

  • message_passing() and scatter aggregations (sum, mean, max, min, std, softmax) for custom layers.
  • Convolutions: GraphSAGE, GCN, GraphConv, GIN and GINE, GAT, GATv2, graph transformer convolution, edge conditioned convolution (NNConv), RGCN with basis decomposition, ChebConv, APPNP, PNA, and EdgeConv.
  • Pooling: global add, mean, max, and attention pooling, top-k pooling, SAGPool, and DiffPool with its auxiliary losses.
  • meta_layer() composes edge, node, and graph level updates into a graph network block.
  • gnn_model() builds node, edge, link, and graph level models with normalization, residual connections, and dropout.

Training and evaluation

  • train_graph_model() trains classification and regression models for nodes, edges, links, and whole graphs, full batch or on sampled subgraphs, with early stopping, learning rate schedulers, checkpoints, gradient clipping, class weights, and a reproducibility record of the settings and split members.
  • predict(), evaluate_graph_model(), save_graph_fit(), and load_graph_fit().
  • Leakage safe splits for nodes, edges, edge labels, and graphs (random, stratified, group, and scaffold). Link splits treat parallel edges and both directions of an undirected pair as one unit, and remove held out pairs from paired reverse relations.
  • Metrics for classification, calibration, regression, link ranking (filtered Hits@K and MRR), and clustering; evaluate_embeddings() with a linear probe; ogb_evaluate() with the official OGB metrics.

Sampling for large graphs

  • sample_neighbors(), k_hop_subgraph(), node and graph loaders, negative sampling, and corrupted tails for ranking evaluation.
  • cluster_loader() (Cluster-GCN), saint_loader() (GraphSAINT random walks with loss and edge normalization), and ladies_loader() (layer wise importance sampling), used through train_graph_model(loader = ).

Heterogeneous graphs

  • hetero_graph_data() with reverse relations, metapaths (add_metapath()), typed neighbor sampling, and typed link splits.
  • hetero_conv() with sum, mean, or semantic attention across relations, and hetero_gnn_model() with per relation SAGE, GraphConv, or GAT layers, RGCN, HGT (hgt_conv()), and HAN.

Temporal graphs

  • Event based temporal graphs, snapshots, and strictly causal temporal neighbors.
  • Temporal graph networks (tgn_model(), train_tgn()) with node memory and time, graph sum, or multi layer graph attention embeddings.
  • Dynamic link prediction with a graph GRU or a GRU variant of EvolveGCN-O (evolve_gcn_cell()), and spatiotemporal forecasting.
  • predict() for temporal fits uses only information available before the prediction time; temporal fits can be saved and loaded.
  • HGT relative temporal encoding and continuous depth graph neural ODE blocks (graph_ode_block(), graph_ode_model()).

Graph transformers

  • Laplacian and random walk positional encodings and shortest path distances.
  • graph_transformer_model(): a Graphormer style transformer with shortest path and edge feature attention biases.
  • gps_layer(): GPS layers combining local message passing with global attention, exact or linear (linear_attention(), with positive random feature (Performer style) and elu kernels).

Explainability

  • Saliency, integrated gradients, edge gradients, occlusion, GNNExplainer, PGExplainer (pg_explainer()), SubgraphX (subgraphx()), and attention weights.
  • Explanation subgraphs, fidelity, and stability measures.

Datasets

  • Built in: Zachary’s karate club, stochastic block models, and synthetic graph, heterogeneous, temporal, spatiotemporal, and molecular datasets.
  • Downloaders with checksum verification for TU datasets and the LINQS citation graphs (Cora, CiteSeer, Pubmed); no third party data is bundled.
  • Readers for OGB node and graph property datasets with their official splits.
  • molecule_graph() builds molecular graphs from atoms and bonds.

Optional integrations

  • graph_diffusion() simulates diffusion on a graph with the modelcompR ODE solvers.
  • graph_operator_symbolic() returns exact adjacency, Laplacian, and GCN operators as symcompR matrices.
  • consistent_labels() finds the most probable labeling that satisfies edge rules with the z3r optimizer.
  • select_links() chooses links under a budget as a 0-1 program in optcompR.
  • aggregate_jax() performs neighborhood aggregation with jaxR arrays.
  • luz_node_dataloader() and luz_node_module train node models with luz; augment() and glance() summarize fits for tidymodels.
